utterances.text: "Therefore, we hold the position of a principled participant supporting a peaceful resolution of the crisis, and we invested maximum efforts to ensure that the principle platform is defined. The delegation of Yugoslavia has a completely different attitude to the issue of maps, military agreement and other specific issues which, precisely on the basis of the principles we have supported, really ought to be negotiated by these three sides. Our position should in principle favour peace and the consensus of all three sides and equal protection of interests of all three nations. But the concrete agreement based on those principles and based on our principled approach to these issues, is in their hands." Therefore, Mr. Jovanovic, specific agreement is in the hands of three sides in Bosnia. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I continue to quote: "Therefore, we support all those three sides in their efforts to sit down and agree on specific issues - maps and other military and other issues." Please, was this the standpoint I advocated, and was this something that was the constant policy advocated by Serbia?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not only in the case of Republika Srpska but the RSK. We were supporting a peaceful and principled solution, and it was up to the sides in the dispute to solve specific issues, especially those pertaining to maps and organisation. This was repeatedly expressed to the international representatives and all those interested. They kept asking you to politically support their efforts, and you did so. This can be seen from the fact that you supported all five peace proposals from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear, but this is not only support for the Vance-Owen Plan, it also shows that we support a peaceful solution and all three sides sitting down together and agreeing on specific issues.

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in fact the issue of maps which is what interested the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But do you recall -- it says that the delegation of Yugoslavia, with respect to issues of maps, military agreements and other specific issues based on the principles we advocated, felt that this was really something to be negotiated by all three sides. This is something we did not want to interfere in. We felt the three sides should agree among themselves. We supported all three sides sitting down together and agreeing on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was the principled approach at the meeting where the Yugoslav representatives were sitting, not the Muslims or the other sides but the Serbs and the Montenegrins. Is this so?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was an honest approach to the problems. This was not in order to present a pretty picture to foreigners, this was what you really wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just put these documents in order. There is a vast quantity of material here presented by Mr. Nice. I have no objection to that, but it's quite time-consuming. Mr. Jovanovic, I will now very briefly touch upon the question put to you by Mr. Nice, who spent an hour going through various tabs showing information pertaining mainly to the content of the draft Resolution of the Security Council dealing with the events in Srebrenica. I will not mention the tabs because Mr. Nice has put them under seal, but the contents were mainly about the draft Resolution of the Security Council in connection with Srebrenica. Mr. Jovanovic, my question is the following: The draft Resolutions of the Security Council, are these public documents?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The draft Resolutions should not be public documents unless they were leaked to someone who was interested in seeing them. Their purpose was for the governments that were to be consulted to be informed and to prepare the final text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but am I right in assuming that these drafts are not a secret to UN officials and officials working in UN missions, that is, for diplomatic staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they should be, but privately they could obtain these drafts in order to gain time and study them thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We will not going into this further. But you received this information because it was available to diplomatic staff who informed you about these Resolutions?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not in dispute?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nice spent a lot of time establishing that you, as far as I can recall from his cross-examination, were informed of the contents of this Resolution concerning the situation around Srebrenica at the latest by the 13th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the telegram that arrived. At least, that's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you were informed about this on the 13th of July and you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I confirm that I received a telegram from a certain diplomatic office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And in response to his question about when and how you learned about the events in Srebrenica, you first replied that the first you heard of it was from the press.

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was established here that pursuant to information that you received, you should have known this on the 13th of July. Is this in dispute?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If it's not in dispute and you said that you found out about it from the press, I have before me a photocopy of the leading Yugoslav newspaper, Politika, of the 11th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "July," interpreter's correction. The 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where on page 3 it says: "Security Council session discusses situation in Srebrenica. The council demands that all sides respect the status of the protected area." It goes on to say that after the session, Hernando Martinez Marco [phoen], the chairman of the council, said that the council was concerned by the worsening of the situation in Srebrenica and its surroundings. I will now let you take a look at this. Let me first quote it and then it can be put on the ELMO. This is a report from New York of the 11th of July, two days before Mr. Nice's document put forward as information, which is quite mystified. Mr. Ahmet Favci [phoen], who said that Muslims last week killed a member of UNPROFOR and threw a hand grenade on an APC of the peace forces, and so on and so forth. You can put this on the ELMO. This is on the right-hand side. It's only partly illegible, the photocopy, because it was faxed. But I do apologise, before we put this on the ELMO, there is also a communique from the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska of the 10th of July where, according to the agency reports, it says that the combat operations are aimed only at neutralising Muslim terrorists and not against the civilian population and members of UNPROFOR. Please put this on the ELMO. What I said is underlined, what Favci says. The date is the 11th of July. This Mr. Facvi, the UN spokesperson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please help the usher to put the right-hand side on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what is the caption? What is the heading?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he can move it down and to the left, please. Down. Not up, down. Down. It says: "Session of the Security Council," and then the main heading is, "Discussion on the situation in Srebrenica." Sub-heading, "The council demands that all sides respect the status of the protected areas." And the part that is marked is Hernando Martinez saying that the council received with concern information on the worsening situation in Srebrenica. And then if you can lift it up a little so we can see the bottom of the page. The underlined part down here. A little bit more, yes. At the bottom you have a passage which says, "Favci confirmed that the Muslims over the past weekend in Srebrenica killed a member of UNPROFOR and threw a hand grenade on an APC of the peace forces." This was published in the newspapers on the 11th of July, and the news item is evidently from the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you must ask a question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, before you received this material with information on the contents of the Security Council Resolution that was placed under seal by Mr. Nice, were you able to see this previously in the newspapers, like all citizens? Not only you but everybody who was able to buy a newspaper, and it was probably broadcast on the electronic media the day before.

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes, because I read Politika regularly. So if it's in Politika, then I probably did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So certainly the information reached the newspapers before you received that information from New York?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the front page of this newspaper - and I will ask you to put this on the ELMO as well, I will give it to you - there is an interview, my interview to the weekly Time, which was published a day before. The title is "Milosevic: Only one solution for Bosnia and Herzegovina, the one that will equally protect the interests of the Serbs, Muslims, and Croats." I'll let you put it on the ELMO in just a minute. I only have this one copy. Let me read a quote. Do you know that at the time the issue of the removal of sanctions, of the lifting of sanctions was being discussed?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that there had already been a decrease in the sanctions?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a result of the 4th of August, 1994. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this show that the international community was recognising that we were leading a peaceful policy?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Otherwise, they would not have reduced the sanctions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was put here, and this has to do with the release of hostages, and they say that I managed to convince the leadership over there to do that, just a brief quotation: "Milosevic: Until the sanctions are lifted, Izetbegovic will count on Serbia collapsing under the weight of the sanctions. It doesn't matter to the Muslims whether this will happen in two years or 20. They're dreaming of a situation in which we will collapse and then with all their allies they will achieve their goal of establishing a Muslim state in Europe. On the other side, the leadership in Pale, since we have been under sanctions, have been counting on us interfering in that war. If the sanctions are lifted and if the relations of the main factor of stability, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, are normalised, Izetbegovic and Karadzic will have to face each other and negotiate a peace agreement without calculating any further as to what might happen." Would you please put this on the ELMO. Would you please help the usher put this on the ELMO, first the caption and then what it says about sanctions and what my standpoint is. "Milosevic: Only one solution for Bosnia and Herzegovina, a solution that will equally protect the interests of Serbs, Muslims, and Croats." And then it says: "Why was it good to preserve Yugoslavia for all Serbs, all Croats, all Muslims, and all Slovenians as our common state?" And then at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the question, Mr. Milosevic? Question. Question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic -- could you just lift this up a little bit so we can see what it says at the bottom. Was this the essence of our policy in advocating a solution -- more, more. Yes. Lift it up a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You will have to reformulate that. You're giving the witness the answer, so --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, what I said in my interview to Time was published in its entirety by Politika, the leading Yugoslav newspaper. Was this my public standpoint addressed both to the international community and in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the quintessence of our policy regarding the Bosnian crisis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you will finish in -- within 14 minutes -- ten minutes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit both newspaper cuttings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, those may be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please take a look -- take a look at the Politika daily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the Court Deputy will give the exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next exhibit number is D276. First Article, D276; and the second one, D277.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I also have a photocopy of the same daily, Politika daily, of the 12th of July. So still within the period of time that you were questioned about as to when the session was convened. Now, on page 1, the Security Council about the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and sub-heading says: "The fall of Srebrenica has been confirmed." And then the UN spokesperson, Mr. Favci, said, "We can confirm that the Serb forces have entered Srebrenica." And now the next sentence says: "What is the Security Council going to say about the protected zones?" And now the words of Mr. Favci, who is the spokesman of Boutros-Ghali -- I will skip over some of the words, although I suggest that you read them all. And then it says: "We should not forget --" I marked that at the bottom of the page -- "that both sides contributed to the deterioration of the situation in Srebrenica and that Boutros-Ghali on a number of occasions demanded that the protected zones be demilitarised. However, that was not done, said Favci." The statement of Mr. Favci goes on to the second page. However, if you put these two pages together, you will see what I just read out in its entirety. Then they quote the following: " Marasin [phoen], representative of the US foreign affairs ministry -- or, rather, Russian foreign affairs ministry said the same thing as Mr. Favci, namely that the attacks on the positions of the Serb army have significantly raised tensions in Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To what purpose are you reading out these passages? It's time for a question. We haven't yet reached the stage where you can give evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, Mr. Nice on the other day spent an entire hour in order to explain how is it that Mr. Jovanovic learned about the events in Srebrenica at the latest on the 13th of July. I just showed you what the papers printed on the 11th and 12th of July, bringing words of UN officials describing problems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the point is that you are not to give evidence. If you read out a passage from the newspaper, you must ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make a point? I certainly didn't spend an hour dealing with the particular circumstances of the arrival of information about the events of Srebrenica. A few minutes. I spent time producing a flow of information of a general character into Belgrade, and I made that clear on several occasions. I haven't stopped the re-examination on the newspapers for two reasons. There may be some relevance or tangential relevance, and it remains a matter for the accused how he spends his time. But it may help the accused to have in mind that if he wants to get material like newspaper reports of his statements into evidence, if he instructs his associates to approach me, it may be possible that I can agree about matters of that sort going into evidence and saving him time. I have been able just to speak to his associates, although I understand their position may be sensitive, but it's perfectly possible to negotiate with me and I will do everything I can to accommodate the appropriate production of evidence without taking time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nice. Mr. Milosevic, you will have note of that offer. You're to put a question now on the passage that you had read.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, was it known to UNPROFOR and to the officials at the Security Council as well as the Secretary-General that demilitarisation was not carried out and that there were many terrorist attacks launched from Srebrenica resulting in many deaths? Was that known?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was known. The Russian delegation, starting in 1993 and onwards, insisted in the Security Council that the concept of protected zone be cleared. That's how they framed it. And the Security Council kept postponing that. It was obvious that the protected zones were abused by the Muslims who used it as a site to launch their attacks against Serb villages. And in the course of those operations, almost 2.000 Serb civilians in the villages surrounding Srebrenica died as a result of those attacks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, are you saying that prior to the fall of Srebrenica you were aware of attacks by Muslims against Serbs but unaware of attacks by Serbs against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew about both. Why wouldn't I know? Those were publicly available facts. It was reported by the media that the Muslim garrison in Srebrenica raided and massacred civilians in Serb villages. It was also reported that the forces of Republika Srpska attacked Srebrenica trying to enter it on a number occasions. That was prevented by the pressure from the international community and also by the pressure exerted by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that day, the spokesperson of Radovan Karadzic gave a statement to the effect that in the past 45 days, they had over 30 civilian victims because the Muslims had abused the status of protected zones and started attacks against civilians. This is what is reported by the papers on the 12th. Were those facts known to the public?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this was reported by the media, then yes, it was known to the public.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I would like this to be exhibited. You can see that the date is the 12th of July. The leading Yugoslav daily Politika reports about the fall of Srebrenica being confirmed. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- if you wish to clarify anything further, we can put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it may be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D278.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, Mr. Nice presented to you tab 21, which deals with the issues of Srebrenica, and it's from April 1993. This is Mr. Nice's tab 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, are you going to deal with it in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need for that, Mr. Kwon. This is not protected for its contents but, rather, for its form. I will not deal with the form, only with the contents. This refers to the Security Council's Resolution from 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Resolution of the Security Council, as is stated here, demands that the paramilitary forces of Bosnian Serbs cease with their attacks on Srebrenica immediately. Do you remember, what was our position regarding these attacks on Srebrenica? As far as I remember, it was not a protected zone yet, or perhaps it was. Was it or wasn't it? And when it became a protected zone, at whose initiative it was done, and who invested maximum efforts to prevent any kind of a conflict in Srebrenica and around it?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srebrenica became a protected zone at the initiative of some Security Council members. Our position was in respect of all protected zones, not only Srebrenica, not to touch them and not to take control of them. This was reiterated publicly by the leadership of the state. Not only because it could have led to a retaliation, but also because we wanted to limit and put an end to the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, not flame it further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jovanovic. Now, please take a look at the document in tab 21 which shows that even at that time, in 1993, the Security Council adopted a decision to introduce the security zone.

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It became a protected zone that year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what activities we pursued in order to protect that area?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember much about that. I just remember that we always warned them about not expanding military action but, rather, to turn to a political resolution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This will be your last question. As I indicated, we are stopping at 1.43.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, we provided assistance to Republika Srpska. Now, please tell me the following: Was our assistance to Republika Srpska something that ever pertained to any paramilitary formations, and did the leadership of Republika Srpska ever ask us to provide any kind of paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was never the case. They never mentioned any paramilitary formations in their conversations with us, only their army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was my position, the position of the leadership of the Republic of Serbia and Yugoslavia, with respect to paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: VLADISLAV JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your position was always a negative one. In talks with us and in talks with others, you always insisted that all those volunteers who at the early stage of the Yugoslav crisis signed up always ought to be under the control of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. And thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. That concludes your testimony. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may leave.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I did not conclude my additional examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I concluded it. It's 1.43, and I had indicated last week that we have to stop at 1.43 so that we don't overrun and so that the trial which is scheduled to begin at 2.15 does not begin at 2.25. I have received numerous complaints.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May tabs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have more questions to ask of this witness? Do you want this witness to return tomorrow, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. I need to conclude my re-examination. Mr. Robinson, are you aware of the fact just how much material Mr. Nice introduced in his cross? At least three times what I introduced in my examination-in-chief. Therefore, I have to deal with the documents presented by him. I have to put questions to the witness about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I was really thinking of the witness's own welfare. He has been here for such a long time. Mr. Jovanovic, Mr. Milosevic needs you tomorrow. You will have to return tomorrow, and I hope your re-examination will be concluded very quickly. I had thought we had finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before I forget, tabs 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 49 and 50 should be under seal, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We are adjourned, and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.
